title: revloop reviewer definition
description: One reviewer definition. The five built-ins under reviewers/ use this format, and so does a file you pass with --config <path>. The file name is the reviewer's name and must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$. A reviewer is one of two kinds, and the required keys differ; see `kind`.

command.description: A subprocess command may not begin with git, gh or the {reviewModel} placeholder. Permission rules match a string prefix, and the local commands grant Bash(git:*) and four gh rules, so such a command would run without a prompt. The match is on the string, so gitlint and gh-review are rejected too: configure such a reviewer as a skill, or rename it. The procedure checks the expanded string again before running it.

kind.description: Absent means github-comment. github-comment is driven by posting a trigger to a pull request, and requires botLogin. local-command is driven by running a review command on this machine, and requires invoke and command. Keys that belong to the other kind are rejected.

invoke.description: local-command only. subprocess runs `command` as a shell command line and reads its stdout: the reviewer has its own context, and its model can be set in the command. skill invokes `command` as a skill in this session, on the session's model, so --model aborts with reason=no-model-boundary. Prefer subprocess.

command.description: local-command only. With invoke=skill, a skill name matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*(:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)?$. With invoke=subprocess, a command line: it is printed in the step 1 table before it runs and is never pre-approved. Put any effort or focus argument in this string. Write {reviewModel} where the command takes its model; the local loop expands it to the value of --model, or to sonnet. The command supplies its own flag, as in `claude --model {reviewModel}`. A command with no placeholder is not pinned to a model.

requiresPr.description: local-command only. True when the review command reads an open pull request and cannot run without one. The local loop then publishes before every round; otherwise it publishes once, after the loop converges. Under --no-publish, step 1 asks you to confirm that a pull request exists, and zero findings from such a reviewer are not read as clean.

trigger.description: Posted verbatim to GitHub. Control characters are rejected, and so is a value that already contains 'revloop:trigger'. A github-comment reviewer with no comment trigger cannot be driven; a local-command reviewer carries none.

botLogin.description: Write it with the [bot] suffix. It is stripped before comparing against GraphQL, which omits it.

cleanPatterns.description: github-comment only. Anchor each pattern at the start: a reviewer's clean phrase often ends with text that varies between rounds. The local loop has no clean phrase; a local round is clean when the output parses, none of the abort rows applies and no finding is found.

rateLimitPatterns.description: Both kinds. The pull-request loop matches these against a bot comment's body, and the local loop against the review's output. A match aborts the round and the run does not retry; run the command again later, which re-takes a pull-request round. A bot comment that starts with a clean phrase is not read as a rate limit. Match the fixed part of the message, never a reset time or a count.

severityLevels.description: The severity words the reviewer emits, most severe first. Use what its output carries, which is not always what its documentation defines. severityMap carries these rungs onto revloop's ladder, critical > high > medium > low, so the two keys are required together. A reviewer that emits no severity has neither key; at the minimal and standard levels its findings are graded by a separate subprocess (procedures/severity-grading.md).

severityMap.description: Maps each rung of severityLevels onto critical, high, medium or low, so that a --rigor level means the same thing for every reviewer. Required whenever severityLevels is present. Every rung needs an entry, no entry may name a rung outside severityLevels, a more severe rung may not map below a less severe one, and on a ladder of two or more rungs the top rung must map above the bottom one. Step 1 checks these at the minimal and standard levels and aborts with reason=bad-severity-map. The map is your judgement of what the reviewer's rungs mean; step 1 prints the rungs that block and the rungs that are acceptable before the first round.

expectedLatency.description: Printed in the step-1 table. A verdict far below this range is usually a failure, not a review.

markerTolerated.description: Whether the reviewer still answers when the revloop marker is appended to the trigger. 'no' aborts in step 1: there is no fallback path.

status.description: Printed in the step-1 table and repeated in the final report when it is not 'verified'.
